gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-arme: Friendly and loose, Lemon Milk spaces its rounded capitals wide and draws them with one pen-like line. Noto Serif Armenian follows in a classic serif voice, with big open counters and a gentle stroke contrast that keeps a long page approachable.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-bali: Striking in its wide tracking and rounded, uniform strokes, Lemon Milk leads while Noto Serif Balinese settles in underneath with tall lowercase. The strongest quality here is the thickness gap between the two.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-beng: Rope-thin, uniform outlines and generous spacing make Lemon Milk instantly recognizable, set above Noto Serif Bengali. Its text reads steadily, with hairlines like thread against yarn.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-deva: Noto Serif Devanagari brings short ascenders and a big lowercase body. Lemon Milk is best at round, unvarying display shapes, while the text face handles the moderate stem-to-hairline rhythm that a text serif needs.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-dive: Lemon Milk stretches its dowel-like stems and bent arcs wide, then hands off to Noto Serif Dives Akuru. Its strongest quality is the shift from rigid rods to softly modulated curves.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-dogr: Noto Serif Dogra feels bookish and classic. Over a long page its mild contrast reads like crayon on rough paper, a soft counterpart to the ruler-and-compass precision of Lemon Milk above.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-ethi: Stroke ends that look cut from one ribbon give Lemon Milk its wide, friendly signature. Noto Serif Ethiopic then lays words down as solid blocks, its mild thick-thin shifts smoothing a longer read.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-geor: Wide, round, and pen-drawn all the way through. Lemon Milk has no calligraphic thinning at all, so Noto Serif Georgian, with its coiled-rope lowercase and mild contrast, adds the visible shading the page needs.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-gran: Lemon Milk bends its wide-tracked letters like tubing of one gauge, friendly and striking up top. Noto Serif Grantha answers with etched-glass subtlety, and that shift from tubing to fine line is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-serif-guja: Lemon Milk is best at pencil-steady, rounded display letters spaced wide and friendly, while Noto Serif Gujarati is best at mildly swelling, worn-marker text. Both feel bookish.
